correctness.rationale: The matched original vertices split into A-type/B-type edges. Any mixed induced matching cannot use every original vertex on either side, bounding it by m+n-2; pure types use only m or n edges, strictly smaller for m,n>=3. Equality uniquely fixes a missing row r and column c and all m+n-2 edges M_{r,c}, yielding mn optima. Their pairwise overlap is n-2 for fixed missing row, m-2 for fixed missing column, and zero if both differ; thus replacement costs are m, n and k. The complete threshold graph sequence follows exactly, including connectedness iff t>=max(m,n). Standard-library exhaustive direct-edge and independent compatibility-clique verifiers corroborate parameter examples, without standing in for the general proof.

originality.rationale: Searched the exact graph family, once-subdivision aliases, maximum strong/induced matchings, and exchange-equivalence formulations against research records, accessible historical claims and primary literature. A complete author manuscript for the closest 2013 optimization paper and relevant full HTML content for the 2024 generalized-token-jumping paper were inspected. The first does not treat reconfiguration of subdivided biclique optima, while the second treats universal graph-distance-bounded moves, not the sharp distance-unrestricted batch budget on this optimum family. The threshold theorem is not a corollary of their optimization or universal reachability statements. Unindexed equivalent work remains possible.

value.rationale: The theorem yields a sharp obstruction to optimum-solution navigation, not merely an induced-matching optimum. It identifies an unbounded necessary simultaneous replacement budget in an explicit infinite family of bipartite girth-eight graphs with uniformly bounded average degree (<4), plus distinct intermediate partial-mobility and final rook-graph regimes. The exact graph sequence is a natural answer for batch token-jump local search; the coordinate classification explains why small budgets fail and supplies both sharp witnesses and matching constructive routes.
